name: Narrative Transportation
description: Becoming absorbed into a story -- engaged imagery, affect, and attentional focus -- produces stronger shifts toward the story's own beliefs, more favorable views of its protagonists, and reduced scrutiny of factual inconsistencies within it.
design_relevance_note: The mechanism behind case-study-driven marketing copy, founder-story brand pages, and testimonial-led onboarding -- a story that genuinely absorbs the reader persuades more, and does so partly by lowering critical scrutiny, which is worth naming honestly rather than treating storytelling as a neutral technique.
prevalence_note: The named concept behind 'storytelling sells' as a design/marketing maxim, though the specific term 'transportation' is more academic than the practice built on it.

findings.description: Readers who report greater 'transportation' (narrative absorption involving imagery, affect, and attentional focus) into a story show stronger shifts toward story-consistent beliefs and more favorable evaluations of the story's protagonists, and notice fewer factual inconsistencies in the narrative; experimentally reducing transportation via processing instructions reduces these belief and evaluation shifts.
findings.source_title: The Role of Transportation in the Persuasiveness of Public Narratives
findings.source_venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
